lede: Stanford carries the stronger underlying team rating — +2.0 against -4.6, a 6.6-point separation on a neutral field before home advantage, travel or rest.
EdgeDesk makes it Duke -16.9 before any sportsbook number is consulted, with Duke winning 87% of simulations.
The position-group comparison shows where the separation comes from: the widest measured gap is pass offense, where Stanford leads Duke by 41 places nationally.
Data confidence on this matchup is 79% — high by this board’s standards, so the margin is the strongest part of the read.

favourite.heading: Why Duke can pull away
bullets: Duke is the better football team by 12.1 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 74% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+12.1 pts).
Playing at Duke is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).
Stylistically the matchup favours Duke by 0.7 points: ball control vs front disruption (+0.7 pts).

QB room: Duke 58.4 (#27 of 68) vs Stanford 57.4 (#37 of 68) — 10 places on the national board.

underdog.heading: Why Stanford can keep it close
bullets: Pass offense: Stanford 52.0 (#25 of 67) vs Duke 35.9 (#66 of 67) — 41 places on the national board.
Offensive line: Stanford 54.6 (#17 of 68) vs Duke 47.6 (#52 of 68) — 35 places on the national board.
ETSR (overall): Stanford +2.0 (#30 of 68) vs Duke -4.6 (#61 of 68) — 31 places on the national board.
The outcome range is 15.3 points wide at one sigma — p10 -6.1 to p90 +37.9 for Duke, so a projection of +16.9 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 4%.

items.text: The market disagrees by 7.4 points. The market is not the truth, but a gap that large is more often the model missing information (a suspension, a starter, a scheme change) than the market being wrong.
